chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one subjected to the penal limit (al-mahdud), if he repents, is his testimony accepted? He (peace be upon him) said: When he repents, and his repentance is that he retracts from what he had said, and declares himself a liar in the presence of the Imam and in the presence of the Muslims. So when he does that, then it is upon the Imam to accept his testimony after that.

key_terms.الْمَحْدُود: The one subjected to the penal limit (hadd)
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْإِمَامِ: In the presence of the Imam
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: In the presence of the Muslims
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ مِمَّا قَالَ: He retracts from what he had said

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting the testimony of someone who repents after being subjected to a penal limit (hadd)?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that repentance (tawbah) for a slanderer (qadhf) is not merely internal but requires a formal, public retraction before the Imam and the community to restore social credibility. This process underscores the Imam's authority in validating the transition from a disqualified witness to a reliable one, ensuring the integrity of legal testimony. It highlights the communal aspect of repentance, where the Imam's acceptance serves as the final step in reinstating the individual's legal standing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the penalised one (by the Hadd), if he were to repent, would his testimony be accepted?’ So heasws said: ‘When he repents, and his repentance is that he should retract from what he had said, and belie himself in the presence of the Imamasws, and in the presence of the Muslims. So when he does it, so it would be upon the Imamasws that he accept his testimony after that’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is subjected to penalty; then he repents: if his testimony becomes acceptable. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he repents which is retracting what he has said and calls himself a liar before the Imam of the Muslims. When he does this then it is necessary for the Imam to accept his testimony thereafter .
